content:
maria.lopez: FYI customer (AcmeHealth) opened an escalation — after the quant profile rollout to int8_opt for redwood-large-v1 in us-east-1 they see big p95/p99 regressions. They pasted p95 went from ~180ms -> ~520ms and p99 spiked to 1.1s. They included sample requests that reproduce it consistently.

elyse-support: Posted the customer's samples and a short repro in the ticket. Said it started ~2026-03-11 03:20 UTC right after our rollout. Customer is on Dedicated (resv pool id: rwd-dp-58).

maria.lopez: Repro steps from the customer: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large-v1","input":"<long-ish prompt ~1200 tokens>","max_tokens":256}'
```
They say short prompts are fine, long prompts hit the regression.

jai.patel: Initial checks — metrics show a divergence by quant_profile tag. Query: `sum(rate(infer_latency_ms_bucket[5m])) by (quant_profile, le)` shows int8_opt series with heavier mass in higher buckets for sequences >1024 tokens.

tom.chen: Looking at runtime logs on rwd-node-12 (where this customer routes): see a lot of kernel fallback warnings around quant calibration: `WARN kernel_select: quant_op_kernel not found, falling back to fp16_kernel` — but those fallbacks should give *higher* per-op cost, not lower. If fallback happens mid-execution it can kill vectorization and cause p95 blowups.

alice.wang: Also spotted repeated KV cache re-allocs in the same request path: dtype size changed between int8 and fp16 paths, right after we switched quant_profile we didn’t flush cache metadata. That leads to cache hits turning into full recompute for some sequence lengths.

ben.reynolds: Can we confirm whether this is the new calibration file we rolled (quant_profiles/2026-03-10/int8_opt.json, sha: `f9c2a7b`)? The deploy notes included a small calibration tweak to reduce quant error for LayerNorm.

maria.lopez: Yes that's the file. Customer uses long-context evaluation so calibration mismatch could trigger bad kernel paths.

jai.patel: Hypothesis: calibration produced outlier scaling for a few ops causing runtime to select mixed kernels — a mix of int8 kernels and fallback fp16 kernels in the same graph -> poor CPU/GPU kernel fusion and extra memcpy. That explains why short sequences are OK but long ones regress (more ops affected).

alice.wang: Repro on our side: ran the customer's payload against a canary configured with int8_opt and saw p95 510ms, p99 1.05s. Switching that canary to fp16 (no quant) p95 -> 170ms.

maria.lopez: Customer would prefer we roll them back ASAP. They asked if we can toggle per-deployment quant profile.

ops-bot: Incident created INC-2026-042 by @maria.lopez — severity: high — affected: Dedicated pools in us-east-1 with int8_opt profile.

sre-oncall: For immediate mitigation we can: 1) revert the cluster-wide profile to previous (fp16) for us-east, or 2) set a routing override for rwd-dp-58 to force fp16 for that pool. Which is less disruptive?

tom.chen: Route override for rwd-dp-58 is safest and fastest (no full rollback). I can push a route patch that forces model_variant: fp16 on that pool. Command (internal):
```
redwoodctl routes update --pool rwd-dp-58 --set model_variant=fp16 --reason "rollback int8_opt for affected pool"
```
Estimated 5 min to apply + 2 min to converge.

maria.lopez: Do it. Please also set a canary for ~10% of other Dedicated pools to watch for broader impact.

tom.chen: On it. Applying now.

(2m later)

tom.chen: route patch applied. Confirmed rwd-dp-58 now serves fp16 variant.

jai.patel: Telemetry: after override p95 for their tenant dropped to ~185ms within 90s. Tagging metrics: `tenant:acmehealth` and `quant_profile:fp16`. Looks like immediate mitigation worked.

elyse-support: Customer confirmed latency returned to expected range and is happy with rollback. Still wants root cause and a plan to safely reintroduce int8.

maria.lopez: Root cause plan: 1) examine failing ops in calibration file, 2) add validation gate in deploy pipeline that runs long-context workload sims (>=1024 tokens) against new quant profiles, 3) add runtime protection to avoid mixed-dtype kernel mixes in a single execution (prefer all-fallback to fp16 early).

ben.reynolds: On the runtime side I can enforce a conservative fallback policy: if any op falls back to fp16 we force remaining ops to run fp16 for that request — avoids mixed-kernel penalties. Will spike memory but prevents perf cliff. I'll open a small PR.

alice.wang: On the ML side I will re-run calibration with stricter outlier clipping and produce an updated int8 profile. Also create an evaluation job that runs the customer-provided long prompts through quant-sim to measure expected latency and accuracy.

maria.lopez: Action items and owners: 
- tom.chen: route override + canary (done)
- ben.reynolds: runtime fallback policy PR (ETA 6 hours)
- alice.wang: re-calibrate int8 profile + eval harness (ETA 24 hours)
- jai.patel: add canary metrics dashboard and perf regression alert keyed to quant_profile (ETA 4 hours)
- elyse-support: confirm with customer and keep ticket updated

jai.patel: Also adding a Prometheus rule to alert if p95_int8 / p95_fp16 > 1.5 over 10m for any pool. Query suggestion: `avg_over_time(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(infer_latency_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, quant_profile, pool))[10m:1m])` and compare ratios.

maria.lopez: Note for rollout policy docs — we should document per-pool overrides and the rollback playbook. Include examples for `redwoodctl`.

elyse-support: Customer asked if we can run a controlled A/B of the fixed int8 profile against a small sample of their traffic. Proposed next step: once ML produces new profile and runtime PR merges, we do 5% A/B and monitor p95/p99 and quality drift.

tom.chen: Agreed. Will coordinate canary window and add automatic fallback to fp16 if p95 crosses threshold.

ben.reynolds: PR opened: `runtime: prefer-request-wide-same-dtype-on-fallback` — includes test harness that simulates kernel-mix penalty. Link: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/3124 (internal).

alice.wang: Uploaded new calibration artifact `quant_profiles/2026-03-12/int8_opt_v2.json` sha: `a3e9d1c`. Running evals now against long-context benchmark.

(1h later)

alice.wang: Eval results: int8_opt_v2 matches fp16 latency within 5% on p95 for our long-context benchmark and accuracy drop is within the allowable threshold. P95: fp16 172ms, int8_opt_v2 185ms.

jai.patel: I deployed 5% canary to rwd-dp-59 and set automatic rollback if tenant-level p95 > 1.2x baseline for 5m.

maria.lopez: Great. Customer will be invited to the canary. Final ask from customer — we should provide a short postmortem and confirm billing is unchanged (no hidden cost from fallbacks).

elyse-support: I'll draft the customer-facing summary and ensure billing team verifies no invoice impact.

maria.lopez: Thanks everyone. Keeping thread open until A/B is complete. If anyone notices further anomalies ping @sre-oncall. :thumbsup:
